newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firm on dollar inflow.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firm on dollar inflow.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed firmer for the seventh session in a row on Friday as capital continued to flow into Mexico following a smoother than expected electoral process on July 6 and positive economic data, dealers said.
"Optimism following the elections drew in dollars, and this week's data underlined confidence in Mexico," a dealer said, referring to mild inflation and strong trade figures.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 1.8 and 1.4 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.8540/7.8570 and 7.8480/7.8530 per dollar.
Dealers said the strength of the peso could have encouraged dealers to exercise dollar puts previously auctioned by the central bank.
Dealers said Banco de Mexico had auctioned $300 million in dollar puts on Wednesday, in addition to an identical amount auctioned at the end of June.
"Most of the central bank's second batch of (dollar) puts has almost entirely been exercised," the trader added. "The peso pierced a strong psychological resistance at 7.85 per dollar today."
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 3.15 centavos firmer at 7.8390/7.8425 per dollar.
Dealers said the peso could shed some of its strong gains next week.
"I think the party's over and the peso could slide a bit," another trader said.
